source_context:
1: ---
     2: # traefik — install the static binary under systemd, render the static + dynamic
     3: # config, and let Traefik fetch/renew a wildcard cert via Route53 DNS-01 itself.
     4: # Render is always done; the binary download + systemd start are gated on
     5: # traefik_manage_services (false in CI/template-render — no live ACME).
     6: 
     7: # --- Fail fast on a real run with missing creds / base domain ----------------
     8: - name: Assert Route53 DNS-01 credentials + ingress base domain are present (live run)
     9:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    10:     that:
    11:       - traefik_acme_aws_access_key_id | length > 0
    12:       - traefik_acme_aws_secret_access_key | length > 0
    13:       - traefik_acme_route53_zone_id | length > 0
    14:       - traefik_base_domain | length > 0
    15:     fail_msg: >-
    16:       Traefik needs the dedicated `acme` AWS user's Route53 DNS-01 credentials and
    17:       the ingress base domain. Set AWS_ACME_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_ACME_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    18:       + PROXMOX_SUBDOMAIN in Doppler and ensure ROUTE53_ZONE_ID is
    19:       set (reused from aws-infra). Attach the least-privilege IAM policy from
    20:       roles/traefik/README.md to that user. Values are never committed.
    21:     quiet: true
    22:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
    23: 
    24: # --- Service account + filesystem layout -------------------------------------
    25: - name: Create traefik group
    26:   ansible.builtin.group:
    27:     name: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    28:     system: true
    29:     state: present
    30: 
    31: - name: Create traefik system user
    32:   ansible.builtin.user:
    33:     name: "{{ traefik_user }}"
    34:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    35:     system: true
    36:     shell: /usr/sbin/nologin
    37:     home: "{{ traefik_config_dir }}"
    38:     create_home: false
    39:     state: present
    40: 
    41: - name: Create Traefik config directories
    42:   ansible.builtin.file:
    43:     path: "{{ item }}"
    44:     state: directory
    45:     owner: "{{ traefik_user }}"
    46:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    47:     mode: "0750"
    48:   loop:
    49:     - "{{ traefik_config_dir }}"
    50:     - "{{ traefik_dynamic_dir }}"
    51:     - "{{ traefik_acme_dir }}"
    52: 
    53: # acme.json must be 0600 or Traefik refuses to use it.
    54: - name: Ensure acme.json storage exists with strict perms
    55:   ansible.builtin.file:
    56:     path: "{{ traefik_acme_storage }}"
    57:     state: touch
    58:     owner: "{{ traefik_user }}"
    59:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    60:     mode: "0600"
    61:     modification_time: preserve
    62:     access_time: preserve
    63: 
    64: # --- Credentials (root-only EnvironmentFile) ---------------------------------
    65: - name: Render the Route53 DNS-01 credentials EnvironmentFile
    66:   ansible.builtin.template:
    67:     src: acme.env.j2
    68:     dest: "{{ traefik_acme_env_file }}"
    69:     owner: root
    70:     group: root
    71:     mode: "0600"
    72:   no_log: true
    73:   notify: Restart traefik
    74: 
    75: # --- Static + dynamic config -------------------------------------------------
    76: - name: Render the static Traefik config
    77:   ansible.builtin.template:
    78:     src: traefik.yml.j2
    79:     dest: "{{ traefik_config_dir }}/traefik.yml"
    80:     owner: "{{ traefik_user }}"
    81:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    82:     mode: "0640"
    83:   notify: Restart traefik
    84: 
    85: # Build the routers from the single tofu-owned ingress table
    86: # (tofu_data.ingress via traefik_ingress_routes). Single-backend rows are
    87: # {name, ip, port}; the Proxmox cluster-UI apex row is {name, apex, backends[],
    88: # port} — a load-balanced pool over the node FQDNs. Optional per row: scheme
    89: # (default http), insecure_tls (self-signed backend, e.g. Splunk / Proxmox),
    90: # sticky + health_check (pool session affinity + per-node health checks). Every
    91: # row is normalised here to {name, fqdn, path_prefix, priority, servers[],
    92: # scheme, insecure_tls, sticky, health_check, sso} so the template stays dumb
    93: # (and fixture-testable):
    94: #   - fqdn    = base domain itself when apex, else <hostname>.<base domain>
    95: #   - servers = one <scheme>://<host-or-ip>:<port> url per backend (or the
    96: #               single ip), so single and multi-backend rows render uniformly.
    97: - name: Build Traefik routers from the inventory ingress table
    98:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    99:     traefik_routes: >-
   100:       {{
   101:         traefik_routes | default([]) + [{
   102:           'name': item.name,
   103:           'fqdn': (item.apex | default(false)) | ternary(
   104:                     traefik_base_domain,
   105:                     (item.hostname | default(item.name, true)) ~ '.' ~ traefik_base_domain),
   106:           'path_prefix': item.path_prefix | default('', true),
   107:           'priority': item.priority | default(0, true),
   108:           'servers': (item.backends | default([item.ip | default('')]))
   109:                      | map('regex_replace', '^', (item.scheme | default('http')) ~ '://')
   110:                      | map('regex_replace', '$', ':' ~ (item.port | string))
   111:                      | list,
   112:           'scheme': item.scheme | default('http'),
   113:           'insecure_tls': item.insecure_tls | default(false),
   114:           'sticky': item.sticky | default(false),
   115:           'health_check': item.health_check | default(false),
   116:           'health_check_path': item.health_check_path | default('/'),
   117:           'health_check_port': item.health_check_port | default(0),
   118:           'health_check_interval': item.health_check_interval
   119:             | default(traefik_health_check_interval_overrides[item.name] | default(''), true)
   120:             | default(traefik_health_check_interval, true),
   121:           'health_check_timeout': item.health_check_timeout | default(traefik_health_check_timeout, true),
   122:           'sso': item.sso | default(false)
   123:         }]
   124:       }}
   125:   loop: "{{ traefik_ingress_routes }}"
   126:   loop_control:
   127:     label: "{{ item.name }} -> {{ (item.backends | default([item.ip | default('?')])) | join(', ') }}:{{ item.port }}"
   128: 
   129: - name: Render the dynamic Traefik config (routers + services)
   130:   ansible.builtin.template:
   131:     src: dynamic.yml.j2
   132:     dest: "{{ traefik_dynamic_dir }}/dynamic.yml"
   133:     owner: "{{ traefik_user }}"
   134:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
   135:     mode: "0640"
   136:   notify: Restart traefik
   137: 
   138: # --- Dashboard credentials + binary + service (live runs only) ---------------
   139: # Generate the dashboard basicAuth htpasswd on the host (build-time, persisted,
   140: # idempotent) so no credential is ever committed or in the rendered config.
   141: - name: Generate the dashboard basicAuth credentials
   142:   ansible.builtin.import_tasks: dashboard_auth.yml
   143:   when:
   144:     - traefik_manage_services | bool
   145:     - traefik_dashboard_enabled | bool
   146: 
   147: - name: Install the Traefik binary
   148:   ansible.builtin.import_tasks: install.yml
   149:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   150: 
   151: - name: Render the Traefik systemd unit
   152:   ansible.builtin.template:
   153:     src: traefik.service.j2
   154:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/traefik.service
   155:     owner: root
   156:     group: root
   157:     mode: "0644"
   158:   notify: Restart traefik
   159:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   160: 
   161: - name: Enable + start Traefik
   162:   ansible.builtin.systemd:
   163:     name: traefik.service
   164:     state: started
   165:     enabled: true
   166:     daemon_reload: true
   167:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   168: 
   169: # --- Post-deploy: verify Traefik actually ACCEPTED the dynamic config --------
   170: # Traefik's file provider hot-reloads dynamic.yml and, on a parse/build error,
   171: # logs it and SILENTLY KEEPS THE LAST-GOOD CONFIG (or none) — every backing
   172: # host then 404s with no signal. A rendered config that CI's YAML-parse guard
   173: # somehow still let through (or an env-specific breakage) would otherwise land
   174: # live and stay invisible until someone notices the outage. Flush the pending
   175: # restart, then fail the converge loudly if the file provider rejected the
   176: # config, instead of reporting a green run over a dead ingress.
   177: - name: Apply the pending Traefik restart before verifying the config loaded
   178:   ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
   179: 
   180: - name: Give Traefik's file provider a moment to (re)load the dynamic config
   181:   ansible.builtin.wait_for:
   182:     timeout: 5
   183:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   184: 
   185: - name: Read the recent Traefik journal for file-provider errors
   186:   ansible.builtin.command:
   187:     cmd: journalctl -u traefik --no-pager --since "-30 seconds"
   188:   register: _traefik_journal
   189:   changed_when: false
   190:   failed_when: false
   191:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   192: 
   193: - name: Fail loudly if Traefik rejected the rendered dynamic config
   194:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   195:     that:
   196:       # "collecting file configs" is Traefik's wrapper for ANY file-provider
   197:       # config error (YAML parse, unknown key, ...); it never appears on a clean
   198:       # load, so its presence means the live routers were NOT updated.
   199:       - "'collecting file configs' not in _traefik_journal.stdout"
   200:     fail_msg: >-
   201:       Traefik's file provider REJECTED the rendered dynamic config — the live
   202:       routers are stale and every host behind Traefik will 404. Fix
   203:       dynamic.yml.j2 and re-converge. Recent journal:
   204:       {{ _traefik_journal.stdout_lines[-12:] | join('\n') }}
   205:     success_msg: "Traefik accepted the dynamic config (file provider loaded clean)."
   206:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool

     3: 
     4: - name: Include global customer & env_type vars
     5:   ansible.builtin.include_vars:
     6:     file: "{{ item }}"
     7:   with_items:
     8:     - "group_vars/customer/{{ customer }}/main.yml"
     9:     - "group_vars/env_type/{{ env_type }}.yml"
    10: 
    11: - name: Override specific vars given a customer and its env_type
    12:   ansible.builtin.include_vars:
    13:     file: "{{ item }}"
    14:   with_fileglob:
    15:     - "group_vars/customer/{{ customer }}/{{ env_type }}/*.yml"
    16: 
    17: - name: Display applications paths (apps_paths)
    18:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    19:     var: apps_paths
    20:     verbosity: 3
    21: 
    22: # The following tasks goal is to define the `apps` var that describes
    23: # applications to work on.
    24: #
    25: # The first task scans the `apps/` directory of the repository to look for
    26: # applications (services/volumes/configMap & related templates) and store those
    27: # definitions in the `available_apps` var.
    28: #
    29: # Once done, if the `apps` var has already been defined in group_vars, we merge
    30: # `apps` with `available_apps` definitions. This is useful to had metadata to
    31: # services that cannot be guessed while scanning the `apps` directory.
    32: #
    33: # Example: let's say that for your eugene customer, you have defined a
    34: # particular "host" for the "postgresql" service of the "richie" application,
    35: # e.g.:
    36: #
    37: #     # group_vars/customer/eugene.yml
    38: #     apps:
    39: #       - name: "richie"
    40: #         services:
    41: #           - name: "postgresql"
    42: #             host: "pg.foo.com"
    43: #
    44: # While scanning the `apps/` folder, the `available_apps` var definition for the
    45: # "richie" application will be:
    46: #
    47: #     {
    48: #       "name": "richie",
    49: #       "services": [
    50: #         {
    51: #           "name": "postgresql",
    52: #           "templates": [
    53: #             "apps/richie/templates/postgresql/dc.yml.j2",
    54: #             "apps/richie/templates/postgresql/ep.yml.j2",
    55: #             "apps/richie/templates/postgresql/svc.yml.j2"
    56: #           ]
    57: #         }
    58: #       ]
    59: #     }
    60: #
    61: # And the final (merged) application definition:
    62: #
    63: #     {
    64: #       "name": "richie",
    65: #       "services": [
    66: #         {
    67: #           "name": "postgresql",
    68: #           "host": "pg.foo.com",
    69: #           "templates": [
    70: #             "apps/richie/templates/postgresql/dc.yml.j2",
    71: #             "apps/richie/templates/postgresql/ep.yml.j2",
    72: #             "apps/richie/templates/postgresql/svc.yml.j2"
    73: #           ]
    74: #         }
    75: #       ]
    76: #     }
    77: - name: Lookup available applications
    78:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    79:     available_apps: "{{ lookup('apps', apps_paths) }}"
    80: 
    81: - name: Display available applications (available_apps)
    82:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    83:     var: available_apps
    84:     verbosity: 3
    85: 
    86: - name: Display defined applications (apps)
    87:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    88:     var: apps
    89:     verbosity: 3
    90:   when: apps is defined
    91: 
    92: - name: Add meta-data to available applications
    93:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    94:     _app: '{{ [available_apps] | flatten | json_query("[?name==`" + item.name + "`]") | first | merge_with_app(item) }}'
    95:   register: merged_apps
    96:   with_items: "{{ apps | default([available_apps] | flatten) }}"
    97: 
    98: - name: Set applications for this namespace
    99:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   100:     apps: "{{ merged_apps | json_query('results[*].ansible_facts._app') }}"
   101: 
   102: - name: Display enriched applications definitions (apps)
   103:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   104:     var: apps
   105:     verbosity: 2
   106: 
   107: # If the playbook is invoqued with the apps_filter extra var, we restrict apps
   108: # to the list passed as an argument, e.g.:
   109: #
   110: #     $ ansible-playbook foo.yml -e "apps_filter='richie,edxapp'"
   111: #
   112: # This task will build the jmespath query to restrict apps to the selected
   113: # one(s), e.g.:
   114: #
   115: #    [?name=='richie' || name=='edxapp']
   116: - name: Set app filtering query

   118:     # We use escaped double quotes in the first regex_replace filter to be able
   119:     # to add single quotes around app name in the query
   120:     apps_filter_query: "[?{{ apps_filter.split(',') | map('regex_replace', '([\\w-]+)', \"name=='\\1'\") | join(' || ') }}]" # noqa jinja[spacing]
   121:   when: apps_filter is defined and apps_filter | length > 1
   122: 
   123: - name: Filter apps
   124:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   125:     apps: "{{ apps | json_query(apps_filter_query) }}"
   126:   when: apps_filter_query is defined
   127: 
   128: - name: Display selected applications (apps)
   129:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   130:     var: apps
   131:     verbosity: 1
   132: 
   133: - name: Run tasks for apps
   134:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/run_tasks_for_apps.yml
   135:   vars:

   137:       - tasks/set_vault_for_app

    20: 
    21: # Nodes are joined first with CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE "none", so a node whose
    22: # Longhorn CSI plugin never came up stays latent — it looks Ready and nothing
    23: # demands a volume from it — until ClusterForge is deployed days later. The
    24: # failure then surfaces as a five-minute `kubectl wait` timeout on
    25: # openbao-init-job, four layers above the actual cause. Checking CSI driver
    26: # registration up front names the bad node instead.

    29:     set -o pipefail

    31:     nodes=$($KUBECTL get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}')

    39:     for node in $nodes; do
    40:       drivers=$($KUBECTL get csinode "$node" -o jsonpath='{.spec.drivers[*].name}' 2>/dev/null)
    41:       case " $drivers " in
    42:         *" driver.longhorn.io "*) ;;
    43:         *) missing="$missing $node" ;;
    44:       esac
    45:     done
    46:     if [ -n "$missing" ]; then

1: # skip restart if the operator deferred restarts LFOps-wide (lfops__skip_restart_handlers), if
     2: # the service was just started (redundant), or if the user wants it stopped.
     3: # __elasticsearch__service_state_result is registered on a dedicated state-only task (not the
     4: # enabled task), so that enabled-only changes don't prevent the restart.

    11:   when:

    13:     - '__elasticsearch__service_state_result is not defined or __elasticsearch__service_state_result is not changed'
